content:
Two Lyndon B. Johnson High School seniors are heading into the UIL Area G Marching Band Competition this Saturday with the Mighty Wolf Band — and, according to United ISD, with futures in music already taking shape.

Bass clarinetist Mikel Salazar and percussionist Emma Buckley have both played in UISD schools since sixth grade, the district reports. Salazar followed friends into band and stayed after discovering an aptitude for the bass clarinet and the satisfaction of improving through practice. He hopes to study music at Texas A&M University–Kingsville and become a professional orchestral musician, with teaching — as a university professor or high school band director — also in view.

Buckley grew up in a family where, as she put it to the district, everyone was expected to know at least one instrument. She credits percussion's range of instruments, techniques and styles for pulling her in, and she hopes to teach music at the university level, with a doctoral degree in view. She has applied to several universities, according to the district.

Both seniors credit their band directors with shaping them as musicians and as people, and both point to the friendships built through band as among the most meaningful parts of the experience. The Mighty Wolf Band enters Saturday's competition after earning a Division I — Superior rating at the annual UIL Region Marching Evaluation, the district reports.

Sources:

  • United ISD, "From the Marching Field to the Music Classroom: LBJ Seniors Find Their Calling Through Band," October 31, 2026

title: From the marching field to music careers: two LBJ seniors head to area competition
